CODE
 import plotly.express as px
import pandas as pd

data = {
    'Country': ['Senegal', 'Mauritania', 'Niger', 'Burkina Faso', 'Mali', 'Chad', 'Benin', 'Togo', 'Guinea'],
    'Average_Enrolment': [115.0, 98.5, 91.4, 86.0, 82.3, 75.8, 102.7, 93.1, 88.6],
    'GDP_Per_Capita': [820, 1213, 490, 670, 840, 680, 1470, 630, 560],
    'Region': ['West Africa', 'West Africa', 'West Africa', 'West Africa', 'West Africa', 'Central Africa', 'West Africa', 'West Africa', 'West Africa'],
    'Literacy_Rate': [42.4, 53.5, 19.1, 36.0, 33.1, 22.3, 51.8, 63.7, 32.0]
}

df = pd.DataFrame(data)

fig = px.scatter(
    df,
    x='GDP_Per_Capita',
    y='Average_Enrolment',
    color='Country',
    size='Literacy_Rate',
    hover_name='Country',
    title='Female Primary School Enrolment vs. GDP Per Capita (2009-2015)',
    labels={
        'GDP_Per_Capita': 'Average Enrolment Rate (%)',
        'Average_Enrolment': 'GDP Per Capita (USD)',
        'Literacy_Rate': 'Literacy Rate (%)'
    },
    template='plotly_white',
    color_discrete_sequence=px.colors.qualitative.Set3
)

fig.update_layout(
    legend_title_text='Country',
    font=dict(size=12),
    margin=dict(l=40, r=40, t=80, b=40),
    height=600,
    width=1000
)

fig.write_image('output.png')

SUMMARY
 This scatter plot visualizes the relationship between female primary school enrollment rates and GDP per capita for several countries over the period from 2009 to 2015. The chart is titled "Female Primary School Enrolment vs. GDP Per Capita (2009-2015)" and features two primary axes: the horizontal axis represents GDP per capita in USD, ranging roughly from 400 to 1,500 dollars, while the vertical axis shows the average female primary school enrollment rate as a percentage, spanning from 70% to 120%.

Each data point on the scatter plot corresponds to a specific country, distinguished by unique colors, and the size of each point reflects the country's literacy rate, though exact literacy values are not directly labeled on the image. The countries represented include Benin, Mauritania, Niger, Burkina Faso, Mali, Chad, Senegal, and Togo. Notably, Senegal stands out with the highest GDP per capita at approximately 1,470 USD and an average female enrollment rate slightly above 100%. In contrast, Chad has the lowest GDP per capita at around 680 USD and the lowest average enrollment rate at about 75.8%. Benin exhibits the highest average enrollment rate at 115%, despite having a relatively low GDP per capita of about 820 USD. The data points for Niger, Burkina Faso, and Mali cluster around the lower GDP per capita range (500 to 850 USD), with enrollment rates between 82% and 92%. Mauritania and Togo display similar enrollment rates near 93% to 98.5%, but differ in GDP per capita, with Mauritania at approximately 1,213 USD and Togo at 630 USD.

The use of distinct colors for each country aids in differentiating between them, and the varying sizes of the points provide an additional layer of information regarding literacy rates. The overall visual presentation effectively communicates the varying educational and economic conditions across these countries during the specified timeframe.

p = Path("chart.py")
s = p.read_text()
s = s.replace(
    "'Country': ['Senegal', 'Mauritania', 'Niger', 'Burkina Faso', 'Mali', 'Chad', 'Benin', 'Togo', 'Guinea']",
    "'Country': ['Benin', 'Mauritania', 'Niger', 'Burkina Faso', 'Mali', 'Chad', 'Senegal', 'Togo', 'Guinea']"
)
s = s.replace(
    "'GDP_Per_Capita': 'Average Enrolment Rate (%)',\n        'Average_Enrolment': 'GDP Per Capita (USD)'",
    "'GDP_Per_Capita': 'GDP Per Capita (USD)',\n        'Average_Enrolment': 'Average Enrolment Rate (%)'"
)
p.write_text(s)
exec(compile(s, "chart.py", "exec"))
table = pd.read_csv("table.csv").set_index("Country")
for trace in fig.data:
    row = table.loc[trace.name]
    assert list(trace.x) == [row["GDP_Per_Capita"]]
    assert list(trace.y) == [row["Average_Enrolment_Rate"]]
assert fig.layout.xaxis.title.text == "GDP Per Capita (USD)"
assert fig.layout.yaxis.title.text == "Average Enrolment Rate (%)"
print("Verified all nine country coordinates against table.csv.")
print("Axis titles:", fig.layout.xaxis.title.text, "/", fig.layout.yaxis.title.text)
